Title: Anwar: World needs fairer financing system to avoid unsustainable debt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for the international financing system to be reformed to make it fairer and prevent developing countries from being trapped in unsustainable debt.
Anwar said the call was important as the world faced rapid changes in the economic and geopolitical landscape, as well as technological developments.
He said many developing countries continued to struggle to achieve economic progress.
"Too many countries are burdened by debt, to the extent that more is being spent on servicing interest than on education or healthcare.
"As such, the international financing system must be fairer and must not push countries into unsustainable debt simply to meet the basic needs of their people," he said in a Facebook post.
He made the remarks while addressing world leaders at the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, India, today.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, stressed the need to accelerate initiatives through the New Development Bank (NDB), expand the use of local currencies in trade and harness the vast potential of the Islamic capital market.
He said BRICS member states should also take concrete steps to address unfair trade practices, share development experiences and strengthen cooperation in emerging sectors, including semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI).
"The green transition must take into account the realities and development levels of each country because not all countries can move at the same pace or along the same path.
"BRICS has a geoeconomic advantage through its vast market, creating opportunities to diversify trade, reduce dependence on traditional Western markets and generate shared prosperity," he said.
However, Anwar said efforts to achieve inclusive growth would be meaningless as long as wars continued to drive up energy prices and threaten the sea lanes that are the lifeline of the global economy.
He said Israel's actions in the Middle East had also caused countries not directly involved in the conflict to bear the consequences through inflation and economic uncertainty.
"Malaysia's position is clear: sovereignty must be respected, civilians must be protected and the world's major economic sea routes must not be turned into battlegrounds," he said.
Anwar said BRICS must have the courage to make its position clear that Israel's illegal occupation, colonisation and violence could no longer be allowed to continue.
"Every human life must be protected regardless of where they are.
"For Malaysia, strategic autonomy means the freedom to determine our own course and the courage to stand by our position when tested.
"As a BRICS partner country, Malaysia is ready to contribute in this spirit," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Helicopter crash: 'I prayed it was not him,' schoolmate grieves for Zainol Afiq
Article:
SEREMBAN: The news of the helicopter crash in Miri, Sarawak, left Dr Muhammad Fauzan Baharum uneasy, but he still hoped and prayed that his former schoolmate was not among the victims.
His worst fears were confirmed the following day when a message in their school WhatsApp group identified 30-year-old Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham as one of those killed in the crash.
"When I heard that a helicopter had crashed, I already had a bad feeling and prayed that it was not my friend.
"But the next day, it was confirmed in our school WhatsApp group that one of the victims was Zainol Afiq.
"I could not hold back my tears when I found out," he said when met at the Bandar Baru Senawang Mosque here today.
Dr Fauzan remembered Zainol Afiq as someone who was always willing to help others.
"When we were in school, he never had problems with anyone because he was genuinely a good person.
"He was also friendly and always willing to help others. Whenever anyone asked for help, he would try his best to help," he said.
He said that although they had established their careers and lived outside Seremban, they would meet whenever they returned to their family homes in Senawang.
[[nid:1532036]]
He said they last met at a football match organised by former students of their school last year.
"I live in Putrajaya, but whenever we happened to return to Senawang at the same time, we would go out and spend time together. He had always been a good person and never changed," he said.
Meanwhile, the uncle of Zainol Afiq's wife, Hashim Mohd Harun, 58, described the father of two as a good and responsible man.
"He was a good and responsible nephew. He was highly committed and responsible towards his family.
"He also never distinguished between his wife's family and his own family," he said.
He added that Zainol Afiq's death was a great loss to the family, saying he was regarded as an example to others for building a career at a young age.
Zainol Afiq was laid to rest at the Forest Heights Islamic Cemetery in Senawang here at 6.04pm today.
Funeral prayers for Zainol Afiq were performed after Asar prayers at the Bandar Baru Senawang Mosque, led by his father, Bee Sham Ahmad, and attended by Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
On Tuesday, a helicopter crashed near Long Lellang in Sarawak while carrying out a healthcare mission to remote parts of the state, killing all five people on board, including four medical personnel.
The other victims were Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, and nurses Jessie Paya Jok and Debra Moset.

Title: Trump turns to golf, family business on Irish visit's second day
Article:
DOONBEG (Ireland): Donald Trump turned his focus Sunday to golf and promoting his business interests, as he wraps up a two-day visit to Ireland during which his off-the-cuff diplomacy has caused another stir.
The US president caught his Irish hosts and the neighbouring UK off-guard Saturday when he waded into highly sensitive political territory by announcing he would "love to see" a united Ireland.
Breaking with Washington's traditional neutrality on the historically charged topic, Trump argued reunification of the Republic of Ireland and UK territory Northern Ireland – after more than a century apart – was "going to happen eventually."
"It may as well happen now," he ventured as he met Irish prime minister Micheal Martin in Dublin, prompting pushback from pro-UK loyalists in Northern Ireland and some leading politicians in mainland Britain.
"Donald Trump is Donald Trump and the president will say and speak his mind as he sees it," UK minister Angela Rayner told Sky News on Sunday.
"But look, we're really serious about the Good Friday Agreement," she added, referring to the 1998 peace accords that largely ended three decades of sectarian conflict in Northern Ireland.
It stipulates that a referendum on Irish unity can be held if the UK government determines a majority there is likely in favour. Republic of Ireland voters would also need to back it in a separate poll.
[[nid:1532028]]
Tight security
Within hours of his surprise intervention on the issue, Trump had touched down in Doonbeg, on the country's west coast, where his Trump Organization-owned golf course is hosting the Irish Open.
The American leader will attend the tournament again Sunday – the main reason for the trip – before later departing for Washington.
Roads were closed and police checkpoints installed near the resort.
Around 30 people protested Trump's visit in nearby Doonbeg village.
Outside the course's clubhouse, several curious golf fans gathered hoping to catch a glimpse of the president.
"It's a once in a lifetime opportunity," 28-year-old Connor McGovern told AFP.
Trump is joined in the remote corner of Ireland by his two sons, Eric and Don Jr, who have managed the family business since their 80-year-old father returned to the White House last year.
The former real estate magnate, who promotes its enterprises at every opportunity, told Martin that Doonbeg was "one of the greatest courses in the world."
Martin assured him at Saturday's meeting that Doonbeg's 784 residents were "very grateful" for the Trump Organization's investment there after it bought the site in 2014.
Some 40,000 fans are expected at the tournament over the weekend, with local hero Shane Lowry favourite to win.
Trump's attendance adds an extra layer of complexity to a security effort that is reportedly costing Ireland 20 million euros (US$23 million). He could present the winner with the trophy on Sunday.
The course – set among dunes on the rugged County Clare coastline – has twice been targeted by pro-Palestinian activists in the past 18 months.
'Conflict of interest'
Police said three women – aged in their 20s, 30s and 40s – had appeared in a western Irish court late Saturday after being arrested for separate trespass and public order offences there.
Around 4,000 Irish and US security personnel were involved in the weekend-long security operation, with anti-drone technology among the measures deployed.
The golf-mad president plays golf most weekends at one of his family's US properties.
He is even scheduled to host December's G20 summit at his Miami golfing resort.
Opposition Democrats in the US have long complained that blurring the lines between his presidency and personal business interests is corrupt.
According to legally required financial disclosures, Trump raked in more than US$2 billion in income in 2025 – the year he returned to power – with a large portion coming from cryptocurrency activities.
That compared with just over US$600 million in 2024.
The White House has aggressively pushed back against claims of conflicts of interest and that Trump has been using his presidency to enrich himself.
The US leader has similarly dismissed criticism for accepting a new Air Force One plane gifted by Qatar – aboard which he arrived in Ireland.
"Since the Civil War, we haven't had a president with a significant financial conflict of interest from a business enterprise," University of Minnesota Law School professor Richard Painter told AFP.
The former White House ethics lawyer warned Trump's conduct could send the message "that the way to curry a favour with the president is to patronise his properties, do business with his companies and so forth."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After BRICS Summit, Anwar arrives in Keralam for second leg of India working visit
Article:
KERALAM, INDIA: After attending the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived in Calicut, also known as Kozhikode, Keralam (renamed from Kerala), today for the second and final leg of his working visit to India.
The aircraft carrying Anwar and his delegation landed at Calicut International Airport here at 4.56pm local time (7.26pm Malaysian time).
Anwar was received by the Consul General of Malaysia to South India K. Saravana Kumar, Consul General of Malaysia in Mumbai Najwa Musyrifah Ramli, Keralam Agriculture Minister T. Siddique and Keralam Chief Secretary Bishwanath Sinha.
Also present were Malappuram District Collector Dr Vinay Gopal, Malappuram District Police Chief Chaitra Teresa John and Chennai Regional Passport Officer Vijayakumar IFS.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied on the working visit by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
From the airport, Anwar is scheduled to meet the Grand Mufti of India, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, at Markazu Saquafathi Sunniya, also known as Jamia Markaz, here to exchange views on community development, educational advancement and interfaith harmony.
Anwar will also attend a reception and Du'a Majlis, where he is expected to deliver a speech, before concluding his first day of engagements in South India.
Tomorrow, Anwar is scheduled to meet Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar to discuss bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Keralam in key sectors, including trade and investment, tourism, healthcare and education.
Anwar's visit to Keralam is aimed at further strengthening bilateral relations and unlocking strategic collaboration in key sectors, including trade and investment, the digital economy, talent and labour, education and regional connectivity.
Anwar arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Modern diplomatic relations between Putrajaya and New Delhi were established in 1957, shortly after Malaysia gained independence. India remains Malaysia's largest trading partner in South Asia, with bilateral trade reaching US$18.55 billion (RM79.33 billion) in 2025.
After completing his visit to Keralam, Anwar is scheduled to depart for the Maldives on Sept 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flying Doctor Service suspension to remain pending helicopter crash probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) in Sarawak will only resume after the investigation into the recent
helicopter crash
is completed and the Health Ministry is satisfied that the operation is safe.
The Health Ministry said
the temporary suspension of FDS operations
would remain in place pending the outcome of the investigation, with the safety and welfare of healthcare workers remaining its top priority.
The ministry said it was carrying out a comprehensive audit covering service-location mapping, compliance by the operating company with required standards and the psychosocial needs of FDS personnel.
"Operations will only resume once the ministry is absolutely satisfied that operational capabilities and the service delivery system are truly safe," it said in a statement today.
In the meantime, the ministry said it was putting alternative arrangements in place to minimise the impact of the suspension on healthcare access in remote areas.
The
temporary suspension involves seven FDS teams
serving 85 localities, with an estimated population of about 14,830 people in Sarawak's interior.
The ministry also said it was reassessing healthcare services to each locality based on accessibility and local conditions, while maximising alternative transport by road and river where possible.
"However, any alternative method would only be used after a risk assessment covering route conditions, journey duration, weather and vehicle suitability found it safe for healthcare workers."
For remote locations facing severe geographical and infrastructure constraints, the ministry said special logistical arrangements were also being made, including emergency medical evacuation (MEDEVAC) support.
It cited Pa Tik, where travelling from Bario Health Clinic can take up to two days on foot.
"Ba Itam, Ba Abang and Long Tebangan are also affected, with journeys from Long Bedian Health Clinic taking between four and 10 hours due to damaged routes and collapsed bridges."
The ministry said it would continue strengthening strategic cooperation with the Fire and Rescue Department and armed forces for high-risk areas and emergency medical evacuations.
It stressed that all healthcare personnel involved in FDS teams would continue to be protected under regulations and policies governing public servants.
The approach, it said, was intended to preserve access to healthcare through risk-based, phased and accountable decisions without compromising the safety of healthcare workers and patients.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police confirm probe into three policemen over alleged RM13,000 extortion
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police confirmed they are investigating three policemen for allegedly extorting RM13,000 from several men in Pulau Tikus here on Aug 6.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the trio, aged between 30 and 48, were detained yesterday and remanded for four days until Sept 16 to assist investigations.
"Police are conducting further investigations into the incident and the case is being investigated under Section 384 of the Penal Code for extortion," he said when contacted.
The case is believed to have involved the complainant and three of his cousins, who went to Jalan Ladang Hong Seng, Pulau Tikus, at about 2.30am to look for a friend's relative who was allegedly detained by police.
They claimed that they were instead detained by the
three policemen
, handcuffed and threatened with being implicated in a Telekom Malaysia (TM) cable theft case if they did not hand over money.
The men, who were allegedly frightened, were forced to withdraw money from an automated teller machine (ATM) on Jalan Burma before handing over RM13,000 to one of the suspects in exchange for their release.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippine ferry fire victims may take months to identify
Article:
CORON: Authorities in the Philippines said on Sunday it could take weeks or months to identify the victims of a ferry fire that killed 76 people, as forensic experts begin collecting and comparing DNA samples from charred remains and investigators determine what caused one of the country's deadliest maritime disasters in recent years.
Some remains were found clustered together in parts of the vessel, said forensic specialist Richard Allan Mangalip from the Philippine National Police, while others were scattered across different areas of the ship, which was carrying more than 130 people and was nearing its destination when it caught fire.
The ferry was heading southwest from Manila to Coron, in Palawan province, a trip that generally takes about 20 hours.
"Most of them are already in a charred condition," Mangalip said at a press conference, adding that authorities could not provide a firm timeline for identification because of the volume of specimens that must be examined. "It could be weeks, or it could be much longer."
That assessment came a day after rescuers recovered 41 additional remains from the ferry, raising the death toll to 76 and leaving 13 people unaccounted for.
Officials said more remains could still be found because investigators have not yet fully searched flooded sections of the vessel.
Firefighters entered the ferry for the first time on Friday after extinguishing the blaze more than a day after it broke out.
Images released by the Coast Guard showed the scale of the destruction inside the vessel, with rows of steel bed frames twisted by intense heat and covered in ash.
Investigators said they had yet to determine where the fire started and were still trying to access key sections of the vessel, including flooded lower decks and the engine room, where evidence may help establish the cause.
A statement from the Maritime Industry Authority, citing survivor accounts, said two explosions were heard inside the vessel shortly before the fire broke out.
A representative of shipowner Atienza Inter-Island Ferries said at the same press conference the company was cooperating fully with investigators and would continue assisting affected families.
The fire is the latest in a string of deadly maritime accidents in the Philippines, an archipelago of more than 7,600 islands, where millions rely on ferries and small boats to travel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia says six killed, 130 missing after ferry capsizes off Java
Article:
BANJARMASIN (Indonesia): Rescuers in Indonesia said at least six people were killed and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo was hit by bad weather and capsized.
The Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 passengers and crew, had lost contact with its shipping company early on Sunday after departing from Surabaya in East Java.
Basarnas, Indonesia's national search and rescue agency, said in its latest update that six people were killed and 130 were missing. It said 107 people had been rescued.
There were 213 passengers and 30 crew members on board, the agency added.
Indonesian Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said the ship had capsized.
"From the information we received, based on helicopter surveillance... the ship capsized but has not sunk. As of 3pm (0700 GMT) it had not sunk yet, but it was capsized," he said at a news conference in Banjarmasin.
Local search and rescue chief I Putu Sudayana earlier told AFP that the ship's captain had reported to its owners before losing contact that the vessel was "tilting."
Rescuers battled waves of up to 2.5m to reach the ferry, Sudayana told reporters.
"It is extremely risky for vessels. Even our Basarnas vessel, which is 40 metres long, is at great risk," he said.
A Basarnas helicopter has joined the operation, he added.
The vessel's last position had been detected in the Java Sea, around 150 km from its destination.
Heri Purwanto, head of the Banjarmasin Sea Port Authority, said the ship, which was also carrying vehicles, lost contact at 2am on Sunday.
"We responded quickly to the incident report... Our main focus and top priority at this time is the safety of everyone on board the ship, and we are deploying a coordinated rescue operation," Heri Purwanto said.
[[nid:1532004]]
'Very shocked'
Rescue authorities have established a command centre at the Banjarmasin port, with paramedics and ambulances on standby, an AFP reporter saw.
Dozens of relatives and friends of the passengers checked a whiteboard where the names of people rescued were being updated.
Jenah, 26, told AFP she came to the command post for information about her older brother.
"I am saddened and very shocked. Until now, I haven't received any more information," said Jenah, who like many Indonesians has only one name.
"He was travelling alone. I hope he survives. I couldn't contact him since last night."
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
On Monday, a speedboat carrying eight people, including five journalists working for local and international news agencies, went missing near a volcano, Mount Anak Krakatau, in Banten province. That search is ongoing.
The journalists were sent to cover the volcano's eruption that paralysed Jakarta's main airport and several others.
Last month, a fire on board a ferry killed one person and left five others missing while 211 were rescued in the Lombok Strait off Indonesia's Bali island.
The ferry had been heading from Bali to Lombok when it ran into trouble in the early hours of Aug 12.
In July, a ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorcyclist arrested after ramming traffic policeman in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A motorcyclist allegedly rammed into a traffic policeman who stopped him for riding without a helmet here today, leaving the officer with a fractured right hand.
The 24-year-old man was arrested shortly after the 10.03am incident during a traffic operation targeting motorcyclists by the district police traffic investigation and enforcement division.
District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the operation targeted motorcyclists who had committed traffic offences, including riding without helmets.
"Police ordered the motorcyclist to stop, but he suddenly rammed into the policeman who was on duty," he said in a statement today.
The injured policeman was taken to Kota Tinggi Hospital, where he was found to have suffered a fracture to his right hand.
The case is being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving, Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties, and Section 322 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Jamil Khir to be charged tomorrow over Tabung Haji RCI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former minister in the prime minister's department Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom will be charged tomorrow over a case linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
According to the court system, he will be brought before Sessions Court Judge Rosli Ahmad about 9am.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) on Sept 10 confirmed that a
former minister
would be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman was quoted as saying that the charge involved a case linked to the RCI report on TH, after the commission obtained the Attorney-General's approval to prosecute.
Abd Halim was also quoted as saying that MACC had recommended three charges under Section 403 of the Penal Code, which relates to dishonest misappropriation of property.
Section 403 covers the offence of dishonestly misappropriating or converting property for one's own use, or causing any person to dispose of property.
The offence carries a jail term of between six months and five years, whipping and a fine.
Meanwhile, in a statement today, MACC said it had obtained approval to prosecute the former minister.
It was previously reported that a
former minister
had been detained by MACC in connection with the TH RCI report.
He was remanded for five days until Sept 6 after Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah allowed MACC's application.
The former minister was then remanded for another two days to assist in the MACC investigation before being released.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Serian, three Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Four areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today, with Serian recording the highest reading in the country at 174 amid the ongoing haze.
Checks on the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed that Sri Aman recorded the second-highest reading at 164, followed by Kuching at 154 and Samarahan at 152.
Johan Setia in Selangor was the only other area nationwide to record unhealthy air quality, with an API reading of 134.
Meanwhile, 48 stations recorded moderate API readings, while seven recorded good air quality.
API readings of 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN to focus efforts on 126 'winnable' parliamentary seats ahead of GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas and its allies in Perikatan Nasional are focusing on preparations for their election machinery in 126 parliamentary seats that they believe have high potential of being won in the 16th General Election (GE16).
PN information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa said that number, however, did not include seats in Sarawak.
He said, while Pas may not contest all 126 seats, the party was ready to provide support and assist "like-minded allies" contesting in those constituencies.
"The election machinery of Pas and PN is focusing preparations on areas with strong potential. No fewer than 126 parliamentary seats with high winning potential are currently receiving attention, excluding those in Sarawak.
"Although Pas will not necessarily contest all 126 seats, it is Pas' principle and practice to assist like-minded allies who contest in those seats later," he said in a Facebook post.
It is not known what Annuar meant by "like-minded allies".
Previously, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had said the party would
set up a special committee
to handle negotiations on political cooperation, including with Pas.
Annuar said the decision on which constituencies and how many seats Pas will contest has been left to the party's top leadership.
"We will abide by any decision. Pas also remains steadfast in developing policy ideas and plans for a more prosperous Malaysia," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man stabbed in back by unknown assailant at Kuala Lumpur market
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man in his 30s suffered a stab wound to the back after being attacked with a sharp metal object by an unidentified person at the Kuala Lumpur Wholesale Market yesterday.
Sentul acting district police chief Superintendent Jasni Zolpa said the incident occurred about 8.40am while the man was working at the market.
"The victim was taken to Selayang Hospital for further treatment and is in stable condition. The victim's friend also lodged a police report about 1.30pm today.
"Investigations are underway to determine the motive for the incident," he said in a statement here today.
Earlier, a 47-second video went viral on social media showing a man in a green shirt in pain after being stabbed in the back with a sharp object.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand weighs flat 450-baht entry fee for foreign visitors by 2027
Article:
BANGKOK: The Thai government is currently conducting a public consultation on a proposed tourism fee of 450 baht (approximately RM55.35) for all foreign visitors.
The Ministry of Tourism and Sports announced that the proposal will be open for public consultation until Sept 28 before submission to the National Tourism Policy Committee for review.
According to Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul, the proposed rate is a flat 450 baht per person, regardless of whether visitors arrive by air, land, or sea.
"The funds raised will go towards upgrading Thailand's tourism infrastructure and safety standards, helping the sector grow without relying entirely on the state budget," he said in a statement published on the Thai Public Relations Department website.
The Thai government expects to begin collecting the fee in the first quarter of 2027, after Cabinet approval and publication in the Royal Gazette.
The plan for a tourist entry fee for Thailand was first mooted around 2019 to 2020. The flat rate of 450 baht was proposed in August this year after revision.
Last year, Thailand welcomed approximately 33 million foreign tourists, which could generate an estimated 14.8 billion baht for the tourism fund.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BRICS offers economic opportunities, reduces Western market dependence, says Anwar
Article:
NEW DELHI: BRICS offers significant geoeconomic advantages in several areas, creating critical mass through a large integrated market and opening up opportunities to diversify trade, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said this would enable BRICS member economies to reduce their heavy dependence on traditional Western markets.
"These synergies, created, explored and optimally harnessed, will serve as an impetus for economic growth and shared prosperity," he said at the BRICS Summit here today.
Anwar said the world could not speak of inclusive growth and prosperity when wars continued to drive up energy prices and threaten maritime routes that are lifelines for the global economy.
He said Israel's aggression in the Middle East had already spread far beyond the parties directly involved.
"Countries that are not involved in this war are also bearing the consequences through higher inflation and uncertainty," he said.
Anwar also said Malaysia maintained that sovereignty must be respected, civilians must be protected and global economic arteries must be kept away from the battlefield.
He said those with the greatest capacity to shape the course of events had a particular responsibility to prevent tensions from escalating further.
Malaysia, he said, hoped BRICS would clearly and unequivocally state what should no longer be disputed: that occupation, colonialism and, more precisely, "settler terrorism" could not be treated as an inevitable fate, and that no life was less valuable simply because of where people lived.
"BRICS can expand our choices and strengthen our capacity to shape the world around us. But influence is not an end in itself. It only matters if we are prepared to use it in support of the principles we uphold.
"For Malaysia, strategic autonomy means the freedom to choose our own path, and the courage to defend that choice when the time comes.
"As a BRICS partner country, Malaysia hopes to contribute in that spirit," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Queen visits man who lost wife, two sons in Kluang house fire
Article:
KLUANG: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, today visited a man who lost his wife and two sons in a devastating house fire in Taman Titiwangsa here.
Her Majesty, accompanied by Her Highness Tunku Mahkota Johor Che' Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Bustamam, visited Khairul Nizam Wahid, 50, and offered support and aid to the grieving family.
The royal visit came after the fire claimed the lives of
Khairul Nizam's wife and their two children
on Sept 9.
Raja Zarith Sofiah and Che' Puan Khaleeda also visited three other recipients and presented them with aid during their visit to the district.
The assistance was part of aid provided by the Queen to asnaf recipients in Kluang.
The recipients included Saimah Samijan, Rajaswary Sakarai and Loh Yee Teng, according to a post on the Royal Johor Facebook page.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After toddler attack, Batu Pahat steps up stray dog crackdown
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A child's recent encounter with stray dogs in Peserai has triggered a wider crackdown, with the local council stepping up operations in villages and known hotspots across the district.
The Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) has captured 736 stray dogs in 205 operations this year, following 1,557 captures in 263 operations last year.
MPBP has also intensified efforts to remove roaming dogs from high-risk areas.
On Sept 5, two-year-old
Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi was attacked
by five stray dogs at about 7am outside her grandmother's house in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, here.
She suffered severe injuries to almost her entire body, was placed in an induced coma and underwent surgery.
The council has stepped up operations at the site of the attack while widening patrols and dog-catching efforts to nearby villages and other identified hotspots.
MPBP president Mohd Nazid Jasiman said
736 stray dogs had been captured
in 205 operations across the district as of Aug 31 this year.
This followed 1,557 dogs captured in 263 operations throughout last year.
He said regular patrols would continue at locations identified as having stray dog problems, with enforcement action also taken following complaints from the public.
Among the hotspots identified last year were Taman Putera Indah, Batu Pahat town centre, Taman Sri Gading, Taman Universiti and Taman Bukit Perdana.
This year, Parit Raja, Taman Putera Indah and Taman Evergreen Heights have emerged as hotspots.
The intensified action comes amid growing concern over public safety, as roaming dogs can pose a risk to pedestrians, particularly children, while packs may also become aggressive when defending territory or food.
Nazid said the captured dogs would be managed according to the Housing and Local Government Ministry's standard operating procedures under the Trap-Reclaim-Rehome-Dispose approach (TRRD).
The TRRD approach involves capturing stray dogs, allowing owners to reclaim them, rehoming suitable animals and, as a last resort, humane disposal of those that cannot be rehomed.
The council would also strengthen public awareness campaigns, dog licensing and responsible pet ownership initiatives.
For a longer-term solution, MPBP is developing its Stray Animal Control Action Plan 2027-2031, covering population control, licensing, enforcement, public education, adoption and neutering.
The plan will also involve cooperation with the Veterinary Services Department, local communities and animal welfare organisations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 30 inmates find purpose through Quran memorisation programme in Machang
Article:
MACHANG: Thirty inmates at Machang Rehabilitation Centre are taking part in a structured tahfiz programme, with two having completed memorising all 30 juzuk of the Quran and another two expected to do so by year-end.
Its director Ahmad Zulkarnain Abdul Khalid said Sekolah Tahfiz Al-Quran Al-Furqan, established in 2023 in collaboration with the Kelantan Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIK), was the first organised tahfiz school provided within a prison facility in the country.
He said the programme had received strong support from MAIK and was formally registered, giving inmates the opportunity to pursue Quranic memorisation in a structured learning environment.
"Currently, 30 inmates are taking part in the programme. Two of them have already completed the memorisation of all 30 juzuk of the Quran.
"By the end of this year, we expect another two inmates to complete all 30 juzuk," he said.
Zulkarnain said the programme was part of efforts to provide inmates with a meaningful rehabilitation process by combining correctional programmes with religious education.
He said while similar tahfiz initiatives existed in other prisons, some were still in the process of strengthening their operations and programmes.
Machang Rehabilitation Centre is a correctional facility run by the Prisons Department in Kelantan, focusing on inmate rehabilitation, skills training and employment
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iraq to reopen Iran crossings after drone attack
Article:
BAGHDAD: Iraqi authorities announced on Sunday a timeline to reopen three crossings with Iran, a day after closing them following a drone attack originating from their shared border on a Saudi pipeline.
After the Friday night attack on the East-West pipeline, Baghdad sacked the military commander in Missan province near the Iran border, after authorities determined the drones were launched from there.
The government then closed three crossings, citing the need to reorganise operations and boost intelligence efforts to stop violations.
Two Iraqi security sources told AFP on Saturday that drone launchers were found near the al-Shib border crossing in Missan.
The government's security media cell said Sunday that "after reviewing operations at the border crossings," they would gradually reopen for passengers and trade on a timeline from Sunday until Thursday.
The crossings are Shalamsheh in Basra, al-Shib in Missan, and al-Mandali in Diyala.
Shalamsheh and al-Shib reopened to passengers on Sunday but not to trade, the government media cell said.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and an alliance of Iran-backed Iraqi armed factions said they hadn't struck the pipeline, though Riyadh had previously accused Iraqi groups of targeting its oil infrastructure.
In July, the United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed fighters in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.
Pro-Iran armed groups have supported Teheran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks on US bases in Iraq and across the region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran authorities say one dead after ship struck in Hormuz
Article:
TEHERAN: A ship was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, killing one person and injuring three, local Iranian authorities said, as Teheran and Washington clash over the strategic waterway.
"A merchant vessel was struck around 5am (0130 GMT) this morning off the coasts of Hengam and Qeshm islands. One person was killed and three others were injured," Qeshm city governor Amir Teymouri said, according to state TV, without specifying the origin of the strike.
Several explosions were reported overnight around Qeshm, the largest island in the Hormuz strait.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations monitor said later it had received reports of a vessel being struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
"A fire has broken out onboard the vessel following the reported attack. Local authorities are on the scene and assisting in evacuating crew members," it added without elaborating further on the attack.
The incident comes a day before a meeting between Iran and Gulf states in Oman, which also borders the strait, over the blockaded route crucial for global oil and gas trade.
Control over the strait has become a major flashpoint in the conflict between Iran and the United States in their six-month war.
In retaliation for attacks by the United States and Israel that started the war on February 28, Iran has blocked the waterway, a passage that was previously free and unobstructed before the conflict began.
Iran now requires vessels to obtain authorisation to pass through the strait, citing security and sovereignty concerns, and is considering a mechanism to impose service fees.
Vessels that fail to comply are frequently targeted by Iranian strikes, while the United States sporadically bombs the Iranian coast in a bid to challenge Teheran's control of the strait.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Remains of Captain Zainol Afiq arrive at Bandar Baru Senawang mosque
Article:
SEREMBAN: The remains of helicopter crash victim Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham arrived at Bandar Baru Senawang Mosque here about 4.20pm today.
Family members, friends and members of the public had gathered at the mosque from about 4pm to await the arrival of the pilot's remains.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was also at the mosque, arriving at about 4.15pm.
The mosque compound and surrounding areas were packed with vehicles, resembling the scene during Friday prayers.
Traffic police were deployed to manage traffic, while Seremban district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman and his personnel monitored the situation.
Zainol Afiq is expected to be buried at the Forest Heights Muslim Cemetery here after the funeral prayers.
On Tuesday, a helicopter crashed near
Long Lellang in Sarawak
while carrying out a healthcare mission to remote parts of the state, killing all five people on board, including four medical personnel.
The other victims were Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, and nurses Jessie Paya Jok and Debra Moset.

Title: Helicopter crash: Remains of Dr Ainul Baraah laid to rest in Pengkalan Chepa
Article:
KOTA BARU: A sombre atmosphere enveloped the burial of medical officer the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Sri Kedeper Islamic Cemetery in Pengkalan Chepa here today.
The burial ceremony concluded at 2.20pm following the funeral prayer at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, which was
led by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad
immediately after the Zohor prayers.
Also present were Health Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased's family members and friends.
Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah's remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at the Sultan Ismail Petra Airport in Pengkalan Chepa, Kota Bharu, at 11.21am.
Dr Ainul Baraah, 33, was one of five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, Sarawak; the aircraft crashed and caught fire near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3.40 pm last Tuesday.
The crash also claimed the lives of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31, and two nurses, Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin welcomes Umno commitment to stay in unity government
Article:
KULIM: Umno's commitment to remain in the unity government until the end of its term is a positive development to ensure political stability, economic growth and efforts to address the people's problems remain priorities, a Pakatan Harapan leader said.
PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's stance was in line with the memorandum of understanding signed between the parties in 2022 to form the unity government.
He also said political attacks between leaders of both parties were normal and could be resolved ahead of the election.
"I was involved in the formation of the unity government as early as November 2022, and I know that, in terms of documentation, we signed an understanding, a written agreement, to work together until the end of the term.
"So when the Umno president said at his press conference yesterday that he would uphold that commitment, it is because, rationally, this government needs to be defended in the interest of political stability so that we can focus on managing the economy and ensuring the people benefit.
"I think that is a good decision and we welcome it," he said.
Saifuddin, who is also home minister, said this when met after attending a visit to the Kampung Badlishah-Ayer Putih, Junjong road construction and completion project here today.
On the criticism frequently directed by Umno leaders at PH, and vice versa, Saifuddin said such remarks could be based on issues that each party's leadership considered important.
He said the criticism had so far not affected the stability of the unity government, with cooperation between the parties remaining intact.
"Exchanging attacks is normal in politics. I agree, I say so. He does not agree, he says so. That is politics.
"What is most important is that its (Umno's) president has clearly said it will remain (in the unity government). We hold on to that first. As for the usual attacks, I do not consider them to be affecting stability," he said.
Yesterday, Zahid, at a press conference after the Umno General Assembly, reiterated the
party's commitment to continue supporting the existing leadership in the administration of the country.
He said Umno also did not oppose any party, particularly the Prime Minister, as the assembly's resolution to remain in the unity government until the end of the term must be respected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dzulkefly leads 1,000 congregants in funeral prayers for Dr Ainul Baraah
Article:
KOTA BARU: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad led the funeral prayers for medical officer, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here at 1.37 pm today.
The prayers were attended by over 1,000 congregants, including Ministry of Health (MOH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan State Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased's family members and friends.
The deceased's father, Kamarudin Salleh, 69, said he and his family had granted permission for Dzulkefly to lead the funeral prayers as a mark of respect.
"I wish to express my gratitude to the Health Minister and the public—including relatives and friends—for their constant prayers and for keeping my late daughter in their thoughts," he said.
Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah's remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at Sultan Ismail Petra Airport, Pengkalan Chepa, at 11.21 am.
The crash on Tuesday claimed the lives of all five individuals on board the Bo-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3.40 pm.
In addition to Dr Ainul Baraah, the other victims were Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and two nurses, Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40.
– BERNAMA
