Title: APEC ministers push for greater energy security in Asia Pacific
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) energy ministers are pushing to strengthen energy security across Asia Pacific as rising electricity demand puts greater pressure on power systems, costs and supply chains.
Electricity consumption across APEC could nearly double by 2060, driven by growing electrification, data centres and changing transport needs,
Meeting in Beijing for the 16th APEC Energy Ministerial Meeting, ministers focused on how the region can meet that demand while strengthening energy systems, widening access and limiting cost pressures on households and businesses.
"The Asia Pacific accounts for roughly 60 per cent of global energy production and consumption.
"Strengthening energy cooperation is directly relevant not only to each economy's own development but also carries significant weight for the global energy landscape." said Ding Xuexiang, China's vice premier, in his opening remarks.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is adding another dimension to the challenge.
In 2025, electricity demand for AI training data centers grew 17 per cent, outpacing the three percent growth in global electricity demand.
At the same time, AI can help energy systems forecast demand, manage grids and distribute power more efficiently.
Ministers highlighted the need for more energy-efficient technologies and talent capable of working across the energy and digital sectors, backed by strong cybersecurity and data protection.
But meeting new demand is only part of the challenge.
Ministers also focused on extending reliable electricity to underserved communities, including through off-grid and mini-grid systems that can bring power to remote areas without relying on extensions of the main grid.
"Energy is a critical foundation for economic and social development. We must jointly improve energy accessibility, delivering high-quality energy services and practical measures to help remote areas and vulnerable groups improve their energy situation," Ding urged.
Affordability was another focus, with ministers calling for easier access to financing that can help households cover the upfront cost of energy-efficient appliances and systems.
Economies also discussed how to meet technology-driven energy demand without increasing costs for local communities, emphasising consumer protection and more transparent rules for electricity pricing and trading.
Supply chain disruptions are also compounding affordability pressures, driving up prices and straining energy systems region-wide.
Ministers deliberated ways to diversify energy sources and trade routes, strengthen critical energy infrastructures such as submarine and power cables and enhance emergency reserve management across the region.
As the region's energy landscape shifts, resilience, access and affordability are converging into a single priority.
The meeting's discussions build on progress towards APEC's goal of doubling the region's share of renewable energy by 2030 and cutting energy intensity 45 per cent by 2035.
The meeting returned to Beijing 12 years after APEC energy ministers met in the city in 2014, when they set the region's 2030 renewable energy goal.
"Twelve years later, the global energy landscape is undergoing complex and profound transformations," said Wang Hongzhi, chair of the ministerial meeting and administrator of China's National Energy Administration.
"Patterns of energy production and consumption are being reshaped at an accelerated pace, presenting a new set of opportunities and challenges for energy development in the Asia-Pacific," Hongzhi added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Skeleton found inside water drum at Durian Tunggal Dam
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Skeletal remains believed to be human were found inside a water drum at the Durian Tunggal Dam catchment pond here at noon.
The discovery was made after a member of the public found the blue water drum and alerted authorities.
Alor Gajah District Police Chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar said the identity of the skeleton has yet to be established.
He said police are investigating to determine the cause of death and how the remains ended up inside the drum.
"The identity of the skeleton has yet to be established and investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of death and how it ended up inside the drum," he told reporters at the scene.
Further developments on the case are expected to be announced by police once initial investigations are complete.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lebuh Pudu raid uncovers suspected clinics serving foreigners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: At least four premises suspected of illegally selling and storing medicines, including two operating like makeshift clinics for foreigners, were uncovered during a massive Immigration Department-led operation in Lebuh Pudu today.
The suspected clinics, concealed behind businesses selling textiles and offering travel services, were equipped with devices used to conduct blood pressure, blood sugar and blood tests.
Authorities believe the premises catered primarily to foreigners and were possibly operated by foreign doctors, although no one was found inside when enforcement officers raided them.
The discovery was made during Op Bersepadu Mega, a multi-agency operation led by the Immigration Department which saw 472 foreigners suspected of immigration offences detained following raids beginning at 11am.
Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Health Department Pharmacy Enforcement Branch chief Shafilliza Samsuri said various medicines without Health Ministry approval were seized from the premises.
"These clinics targeted foreign customers.
"The modus operandi detected was that the premises were suspected of being operated by foreign doctors. However, no one was inside the premises during the raid.
"Initial investigations found that patients would be brought to rooms at the back of the premises to undergo blood pressure and blood sugar tests before being given medication," she told reporters.
Shafilliza said the medicines seized included antibiotics and drugs used to treat high blood pressure and fungal infections.
Authorities also discovered injectable local anaesthetics and sets of needles at the premises.
She said most of the medicines were believed to have been brought into Malaysia from Bangladesh.
"We will investigate who rented the premises and identify the individual who acted as the doctor," she said.
The operation was conducted by the Immigration Department together with the Health Ministry, Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM), Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, Kuala Lumpur City Hall and National Registration Department.
Meanwhile, SSM issued 25 compounds totalling RM66,500 following inspections at 125 premises during the operation.
Among the offences detected were failures to display business names and registration numbers on signboards, official receipts, bills and invoices, as well as failures to display business registration certificates at the premises.
Other offences included failing to submit particulars of changes to businesses as required under the Registration of Businesses Act 1956 and Companies Act 2016.
SSM will also take action under Section 5C of the Registration of Businesses Act 1956 and Section 549 of the Companies Act 2016 over the alleged misuse of business registrations by allowing foreigners to operate businesses.
The Kuala Lumpur Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry also issued 10 compounds totalling RM8,500 for offences involving pricing and weighing instruments.
Enforcement officers also seized 119kg of subsidised packet cooking oil for further investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid has 3 options to challenge unity government
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim said Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has three options if he wishes to challenge the unity government without waiting for the prime minister to take action to remove the party from the coalition.
He said the three options were for Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) MPs to withdraw their support for the government, for Umno ministers to resign from Cabinet, or to table a motion of no confidence against the prime minister when Parliament sits on Oct 5.
He said all three options had parliamentary channels available and did not require Zahid to wait for Anwar to dismiss Umno ministers or remove the party from the government.
"The unity government is not a formal coalition — it is a loose arrangement and any party can withdraw at any time. At the same time, Anwar is someone who is indebted to Umno and would not have the heart to dismiss Umno ministers or remove the party from the government.
"It is unbecoming to be making threats and issuing challenges at the 2026 Umno General Assembly because the people are watching. It would be better to follow the example of Pandan MP Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, who resigned on his own accord.
"Zahid may crow in front of three million Umno members, but do not forget the country has 33 million citizens," he said when contacted today.
Yesterday, media reports said Umno had issued an ultimatum to the unity government: either call the 16th general election to seek a fresh mandate, or formally remove Umno from the coalition.
Zahid said the call was made after taking into account demands that Umno should no longer remain part of the unity government.
Meanwhile, Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies senior political science lecturer Mujibu Abd Muis said if the relationship ended and a majority could no longer be maintained, the dissolution of Parliament could become an option to seek a new mandate.
"However, government support is still estimated at around 120 seats if BN withdraws its support. That figure still exceeds the 112 seats needed for a simple majority, but the margin of only around eight seats cannot be considered comfortable.
"From a purely numerical standpoint, Anwar can still survive without BN, provided PH, GPS and GRS and other government supporters remain committed. The question is not just whether BN leaves, but whether Anwar can consistently maintain at least 112 votes through to GE16, particularly when passing the budget and other important government business," he said.
He added that the roles of GPS and GRS would become significantly more important as both held around 30 seats each, comparable in size to BN based on the current composition.
"But if GPS and GRS also withdraw their support, the government would lose another 30 seats and the number could fall to around 90 seats. At that point, the government would no longer have a simple majority. GPS and GRS would therefore no longer be mere coalition partners but would become among the key kingmakers in determining the survival of the government.
"The decisions of both parties are not necessarily determined by the national ideology of Umno, Pas or PH alone. The main factors are the implementation of MA63, state powers and autonomy, development allocations, infrastructure projects, state revenues, the position of Sabah and Sarawak in the federal government and the stability of the relationship between Putrajaya and the state governments.
"Sabah and Sarawak are no longer merely appendages of the federal government but have growing bargaining power as Peninsular Malaysia faces intense political competition," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKNPk sharpens pupils' digital skills
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Perak State Development Corp (PKNPk) continues to strengthen digital literacy and modern media skills among primary school students through its StratCom Jr. Programme.
The programme, conducted in collaboration with Sekolah Kebangsaan St. Michael (SKSMI), Ipoh, aims to equip students and teachers with digital communication, critical thinking and media production skills.
PKNPk chief executive Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak said early exposure to media and communication skills was important in building a strong foundation in media literacy and critical thinking.
"We want the new generation to see technology as more than just a medium for accessing information or entertainment. They also need to know how to use it wisely, think critically and communicate responsibly.
"That is what we are seeking to develop through the StratCom Jr. programme. It starts with simple skills, but the foundations being built are important in preparing them for future demands," he said in a statement.
PKNPk said the collaboration, which began in 2024, is being implemented in phases through professional guidance and advisory support to help students develop capabilities in managing digital communications and producing structured, creative and effective content.
To ensure that the skills gained can be put into practice, PKNPk also contributed an iPhone 15 together with a set of media accessories to SKSMI.
The contribution will support the school's media team in producing higher-quality digital content and documenting various school activities.
For PKNPk, state development is not solely about building industries, attracting investments or creating economic opportunities, but extends to supporting talent development and people-centric initiatives.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mujahid ready to assist MACC probe into Tabung Haji RCI findings
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Former minister Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa said he was ready to assist investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
He said, however, that he had yet to receive any official notice from the
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
Mujahid, who was the minister overseeing religious affairs in 2018, said he had no problem providing investigators with whatever information he knew about the issues raised in the RCI report.
"I have been ready for a long time. There is no problem. If they want to ask me what I know, I am open to it," he told reporters after speaking at the RCI TH #Stand4RCITH information programme here today.
He said assisting an investigation could take different forms, including being called to provide information or attend an inquiry at a particular location, but he had so far received no official notice for either.
Mujahid, who is also Amanah deputy president, said nearly half of the 14 cases referred for action in the RCI report had already been known when he headed the ministry in 2018, during efforts to rehabilitate TH.
"Almost half of the 14 cases were already known when I was leading the ministry in 2018, and police reports had been lodged then," he said.
He said cases that had reached the courts should be allowed to take their legal course without political interference.
"We do not interfere in court cases. That is the legal process which we leave to the courts and prosecutors, and we respect it," he said.
Mujahid said the nationwide #Stand4RCITH programme was aimed at helping the public understand the lessons from the RCI findings and addressing confusion surrounding the report, rather than interfering in ongoing legal proceedings.
"What is important is that we learn from this so that similar things do not happen again.
"We also need to explain the confusion that has been raised. That is our responsibility through this nationwide tour, while defending the credibility of the RCI report," he said.
The disclosure of the
RCI findings
on TH's management and operations in July triggered a series of investigations and legal action against individuals identified in connection with the findings.
As of today, four people have been charged in court, while several others, including former senior TH executives and a former minister, have been detained and remanded to assist investigations.
Also present at today's programme were Johor Amanah chairman Aminolhuda Hassan, Johor Amanah deputy chairman Suhaizan Kayat and former Johor Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Dr Mohd Puad Zarkashi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former minister Jamil Khir to face three charges over Tabung Haji probe tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — Former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom is reportedly set to be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow in connection with an investigation into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) arising from a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
According to
Bernama
, the court system showed that Jamil Khir is scheduled to appear before Sessions Court judge Rosli Ahmad at 9am.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman reportedly said on Thursday that the commission had recommended three charges against the former minister under Section 403 of the Penal Code for dishonest misappropriation of property.
Jamil Khir was released on bail on September 8 after being remanded for seven days from September 2.
He had earlier been detained after arriving at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya to give a statement as part of investigations linked to findings in the TH RCI report.
The RCI report, made public on July 29, documented management and operational weaknesses at TH between 2014 and 2020 and identified several problematic investments requiring forensic audits.
The report also referred to suspicious transactions and the concealment of information.

Title: MOH assures healthcare access will continue in rural Sarawak after suspension of Flying Doctor Service
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has assured that access to healthcare services for rural communities in Sarawak will continue following the temporary suspension of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in the state.
In a statement today, MOH said the suspension involved seven FDS teams covering 85 locations with an estimated population of 14,830 people in remote areas.
A two-pronged strategy is being implemented to ensure healthcare services continue in a systematic and phased manner, while prioritising the safety and welfare of healthcare personnel.
“To ensure continuity of treatment, MOH is reassessing healthcare service programmes for each location based on accessibility and local conditions.
“As part of optimisation efforts, alternative transport modes via land and water routes are being maximised,” the statement said.
Any alternative arrangements will only be implemented after a risk assessment covering route conditions, travel duration, weather and vehicle suitability confirms that they are safe for healthcare personnel.
For locations facing significant geographical and infrastructure challenges, specific logistical arrangements are being coordinated, including Pa Tik, which requires a two-day trek from Bario Health Clinic.
Also affected are Ba Itam, Ba Abang and Long Tebangan, which require four to 10 hours of travel from Long Bedian Health Clinic due to disrupted routes and collapsed bridges.
“For these high-risk areas, as well as emergency medical evacuation (Medevac) needs, MOH will continue strengthening strategic cooperation with the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM) and the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF), as previously announced,” the statement said.
The duration of the FDS suspension will depend on the outcome of the official investigation by the relevant authorities. MOH will provide full cooperation to ensure the incident is investigated comprehensively.
All healthcare personnel involved in FDS teams will continue to be protected under regulations and policies applicable to civil servants.
“MOH is conducting a comprehensive audit, including a review of service location mapping, operator compliance with standards, and the need for psychosocial support for personnel.
“Operations will only resume once MOH is fully satisfied that operational capabilities and the service delivery system are completely safe,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Parliament Open Day draws record 13,368 visitors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The two-day Parliament Open Day which began yesterday successfully attracted over 13,368 visitors, exceeding the initial target of 10,000 people.
Senate President Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah said the figure represents the programme's best achievement since it was first organised in 2023, while demonstrating the public's desire to gain a deeper understanding of the institution that serves as a symbol of the country's democracy.
“We have many programmes for the people so that the public can get to know Parliament better. This is their house, the house of the people's representatives,” he said at the closing ceremony of the programme here, today.
He also expressed his appreciation and congratulated the Parliament Chief Administrator Datuk Dr Ahmad Husaini Abdul Rahman, parliamentary staff, and government ministries and agencies involved in making the programme a success.
Parliament staff brief visitors inside the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara on the final day of the Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026 in Kuala Lumpur on September 13, 2026. — Bernama pic
Meanwhile, Ahmad Husaini said the goal of the programme is to bring Parliament closer to the people by giving the public the opportunity to see firsthand the atmosphere and processes that take place inside, given that the area is off-limits on normal days.
“A total of 13,368 visitors were recorded throughout the two days of the programme, compared to about 8,600 visitors in 2023. This increase in attendance shows that public awareness and interest in the institution of Parliament are growing,” he said.
A visitor, Ahmad Firdaus Abdullah Tahrin, 43, said he took the opportunity to bring his children and friends to visit Parliament to provide direct exposure to the institution.
Visitors take a closer look at the Parliament lobby during the Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026 in Kuala Lumpur on September 13, 2026. — Bernama pic
Working as a teacher, he said the visit is important so that children can gain knowledge about Parliament not only through textbooks, but also see the conference venue themselves and understand what happens inside the House.
“When we bring them here ourselves, they can see the actual atmosphere and better understand what they learn in textbooks,” he said.
He added that this direct exposure can help children understand how laws, policies, and acts are debated and implemented, besides preparing them to be future leaders. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast in seven states and KL until 9pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in seven states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 9pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said other areas affected are in Kedah (Kulim, Bandar Baharu, Baling and Sik) and Perak (Hulu Perak, Selama and Muallim).
The same warning has been issued for Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Bachok and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, while in Terengganu, the areas involved are Hulu Terengganu, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Besut.
In Pahang, the affected areas are Cameron Highlands, Lipis and Jerantut, while in Selangor, they are Hulu Selangor and Gombak.
Meanwhile, in Sarawak, the areas involved are Sibu, Sarikei, Betong, Mukah and Kapit (Song). — Bernama

Title: Anwar: No country should have to choose between repaying debt and caring for its people
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for a fairer global financing system, saying no country should be forced to choose between repaying its debts and meeting its obligations to its people.
“Many developing countries were facing debt distress or were at serious risk of it, with some spending more on interest payments than on educating their young or caring for the sick.
“No nation should be forced to choose between honouring its debts and honouring its obligations to its people,” he said when delivering his speech at the National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth at the end of the 18th Brics Leaders Summit here today.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said financing must be “fit for purpose”, stressing that meeting basic needs and providing public goods should not leave countries with unsustainable debt.
He also highlighted the role of commercial capital when deployed on sound and sustainable terms, while calling for progress on initiatives including the New Development Bank, local currency settlement mechanisms and the potential of Islamic capital markets.
The Prime Minister urged countries to take concrete action to dismantle unfair trading practices and share development experiences, technical cooperation and training in emerging fields such as semiconductors and artificial intelligence.
On the green transition, he said countries should be allowed to move at different speeds and along different paths according to their circumstances and stage of development.
“We need to invest in technologies such as carbon capture, utilisation and storage as part of our own transition,” he said.
Anwar also described Brics as offering “crucial geo-economic advantages”, saying its vast integrated market could create opportunities for trade diversification and help member economies reduce their over-reliance on traditional Western markets.
“The synergies that are created, exploited and optimally utilised will serve as an impetus for the generation of economic growth and shared prosperity,” he said.
Turning to West Asia, Anwar said inclusive growth and prosperity could not be discussed while war was driving energy prices higher and threatening the sea lanes on which economies depend.
“Malaysia’s position is clear. Sovereignty must be respected, civilians protected and the arteries of the global economy kept out of the battlefield.
“Those with the greatest capacity to shape events bear a particular responsibility to prevent further escalation,” he said.
Anwar said Malaysia hoped Brics would state plainly that “occupation, or settler colonialism or even more in point ‘settler terrorism’ cannot become destiny and no life weighs less for where it is lived.”
He noted that Brics could widen choices and strengthen countries’ capacity to shape the world around them, but stressed that influence was not an end in itself.
“For Malaysia, strategic autonomy means the freedom to choose our own course, and the courage to stand by that choice when it matters. As a Partner Country, Malaysia hopes to contribute in that spirit,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Man hospitalised after unknown assailant stabs him at KL Wholesale Market
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — A man in his 30s was injured in the back after being stabbed with a sharp metal object by an unidentified individual at the Kuala Lumpur Wholesale Market yesterday.
Sentul acting district police chief Supt Jasni Zolpa said the incident occurred at about 8.40am while the man was working at the market.
“The victim was taken to Selayang Hospital for further treatment and is in stable condition. The victim's friend also lodged a police report about the incident at 1.30pm today.
“Further investigations are underway to determine the motive for the incident,” he said in a statement here today.
Earlier, a 47-second video went viral on social media showing a man in a green shirt in pain after being stabbed with a sharp object in the back. — Bernama

Title: ‘This may be my last time’: Abang Johari hints at possible final term as PBB president, calls on younger leaders to step up
Article:
MIRI, Sept 13 — “This may be my last time.”
That was the candid message from Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg as he called on the older generation to make way for younger leaders to carry on the responsibility and struggle of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB).
The PBB president said leadership succession was a natural process and that the party must continuously prepare and train younger members to take over when the time came.
“I’m 76 years old, in four more years I’ll be 80.
“I want to be frank, this may be my last time. We cannot go against nature, even though our hearts may still feel young. Even if we feel young at heart, we cannot go against nature. But I will make the decision when the time comes.
“We are already getting old, and it is time for us to give way to the younger generation to carry on the responsibility and the struggle,” Abang Johari said this in his speech when officiating at the PBB Northern Zone Special Convention at Miri Indoor Stadium here today.
According to him, the party’s struggle would continue despite changes in its leadership, urging members not to feel disappointed when the time came for them to make way for younger leaders.
“Sometimes we feel disappointed when we are replaced. But this is the law of nature, the old are eventually replaced by the young.
“Leaders come and go. There comes a time when we say thank you and allow new people to take our place. But the spirit of PBB must be carried on by those who love Sarawak.
“What I mean is that we cannot go against nature. But PBB will always be there because we have a system to ensure the continuity of PBB,” he said.
He said the younger generation must be properly trained, not only in leadership but also in dealing with society and people of different backgrounds and religions.
“The successors must be trained, trained in how to communicate with people, how to engage with different communities and how to interact with people of different religions, so that there will be no toxicity,” he said.
Abang Johari said he was grateful to have been trained by leaders before him and believed the same responsibility must now be carried out by the current generation towards younger party members.
He said PBB had already introduced new faces, including young leaders, during the previous election.
“Therefore, those of us who are older should give way to the younger generation,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Anglers find barrel with suspected human remains near Machap Water Reservoir
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 13 — A barrel believed to contain human remains was found on a slope by the roadside near the Machap Water Reservoir here today, according to Alor Gajah police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar.
He said the blue barrel was found by three anglers aged between 25 and 35 while fishing at the reservoir at about 11.40am.
“Suspicious of the discovery, the anglers cut a small section at the top of the barrel before finding bones cemented inside it.
“The anglers then lodged a police report and our team arrived at the location at about 12 noon,” he told reporters at the scene today.
Ahmad said initial investigations found that the remains were believed to have been decomposing for at least three weeks.
He said police then sought assistance from the Melaka Fire and Rescue Department to lift the barrel, while the remains were taken to Melaka Hospital for a post-mortem to determine the victim's gender and identity.
“I appeal to anyone who is missing a family member to lodge a police report to assist in further investigations,” he said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder and urged the public to channel any information to the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Anwar heads to Keralam for final leg of India visit after Brics summit
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for India’s Southern State, Keralam (renamed from Kerala) for his second and final leg of his working visit in India after participating in the 18th Brics’ Leaders Summit here.
The aircraft carrying the Prime Minister departed the Air Force Station (AFS) Palam, New Delhi at 2.15pm local time (4.45pm Malaysian Time) to Kozhikode (Calicut), Keralam.
At the coastal town, Anwar will meet with the Grand Mufti of India, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, to exchange perspectives on community development, educational advancement, and interfaith harmony.
As part of the visit, the Prime Minister is scheduled to meet the Chief Minister Thiru V. D. Satheesan and Governor of Kerala Thiru Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar.
The Prime Minister will head to Maldives on September 14. — Bernama

Title: Home minister: New deputy IGP chosen after consultation with King, announcement due soon
Article:
KULIM, Sept 13 — The appointment of the new deputy inspector-general of police (IGP) has been finalised and will be announced soon, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the appointment process had been completed in accordance with procedures under the Federal Constitution, including obtaining the views of the King.
“The process begins with the Police Force Commission (SPP), which I chair together with the committee appointed by the King in accordance with the Constitution,” he told reporters after inspecting development projects under RP1 of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) by the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said several names had been considered and discussions held before the process was finalised.
“Everything has been completed. We have named the candidate and the announcement will be made as soon as possible, either within the next few hours or in the next one or two days,” he said.
On the eligibility criteria for the deputy IGP post, Saifuddin Nasution said all officers holding the rank of police commissioner (CP) were eligible for consideration.
He said PDRM currently has 25 CP-ranked officers, while three others hold the rank in special capacities appointed by the inspector-general of police.
In July, Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, who reached mandatory retirement age, handed over the deputy IGP duties to Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus, who is currently serving as acting deputy IGP.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said the Kampung Badlishah/Ayer Putih Junjong road project near here would provide an alternative route for motorists travelling between Serdang, Kedah and Seberang Perai, Penang.
He said the 12-kilometre road project would reduce travel time by more than 30 minutes, providing greater convenience and delivering a positive impact to residents. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls for unity to counter PAS and Umno’s racial, religious politics
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng has called on Malaysians to unite against what he described as the “dangerous brand of extremist politics” projected by PAS and Umno following their respective party gatherings.
In a written statement today, Lim said the conclusion of the PAS Muktamar and Umno General Assembly had projected politics centred on religious and racial dominance without respecting the “basic spirit and fundamental tenets” of the Federal Constitution and the rule of law.
He said PAS had reached “new lows” by publicly barring non-Muslims from prominent Cabinet positions, while Umno was openly working to undermine the government it was part of by trying to accelerate the collapse of the unity government to save its leaders.
“Malaysians must unite against this dangerous brand of extremist politics and prevent radical policies that can threaten the nation state embodied in the Federal Constitution,” he said.
Lim proposed 10 areas that he said could help counter PAS and Umno while fostering national unity in Malaysia’s multiracial society and greater integration between Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.
These include upholding the Federal Constitution and rule of law, defending democracy and the separation of powers, and protecting the autonomy of Sabah and Sarawak.
He also called for the constitutional rights of all Malaysians to be protected regardless of race, gender, religion or background, alongside measures to generate economic growth, cut red tape and reduce taxes, utility, compliance and regulatory costs.
Lim said economic benefits should be shared more equitably, particularly among the 17 million-strong workforce, through measures to reduce the cost of living and tackle “toxic rentier economic practices and crony capitalism”.
On education, he called for excellence and a merit-based curriculum with a single examination system to address Malaysia’s declining PISA rankings.
He also proposed greater protection for the natural environment and cultural heritage, basic healthcare for all, and wider access to affordable digital education and opportunities, alongside safeguards against scams and cyberbullying.
Lim said investment in physical infrastructure was also needed to provide good roads, strong public transport and reliable power and water supplies.

Title: Kota Bharu police seek man seen kicking young girl in restaurant CCTV video
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Police have opened an investigation paper in connection with a viral video showing a man kicking a young girl at a well-known Thai restaurant in Telipot here.
Kota Bharu police chief ACP Mohd Azmir Damiri said police received a report from a member of the public at about 10.24pm today regarding the video, which went viral on the Threads social media platform.
“The video shows the rough behaviour of a man kicking a young girl believed to be his daughter at a well-known Thai restaurant in Telipot. It was uploaded by the restaurant owner via their Facebook account,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Azmir said the case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
He said police are still working to track down the man involved, as well as the young girl featured in the recording.
He also urged members of the public with information on the incident to channel it to Inspector Nur Faraheen Azman Lim at 011-11136722. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s Brics partnership broadens trade ties while keeping ‘middle path’, says J-KOM
Article:
GOPENG, Sept 13 — Malaysia’s participation as a Brics partner opens up wider trade opportunities with member countries that collectively represent more than half of the world’s population and purchasing power.
Community Communications Department (J-KOM) director-general Mohd Hisyamuddin Ghazali said the participation allows Malaysia to adopt a ‘middle path’ without having to depend on or align itself with any major global power.
“With Brics, we can balance our trade with various other countries. As a small country, taking the middle path is a very good decision.
“In addition, the people of Brics member countries represent more than half of the world’s population and have high purchasing power, so it would be a great loss if Malaysia did not join this grouping,” he said.
He said this at a press conference after attending the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) with the Simpang Pulai @ Gopeng community at the Rapat Setia Community Hall here today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to deliver a National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit in New Delhi, India, today.
The Prime Minister is expected to emphasise the importance of strengthening cooperation among Brics member and partner countries in addressing development challenges, expanding economic opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of technological advancement and innovation are enjoyed more inclusively by all countries.
Commenting on negative perceptions on social media regarding Anwar’s absence from the group photograph with the 11 heads of state attending the conference, Mohd Hisyamuddin said this did not in any way affect Malaysia’s role or official recognition.
“The 11 Brics member countries are official members. Malaysia, as a Brics partner, remains directly involved in the trade sector. This is an opportunity for us to establish close ties directly with Russian President Vladimir Putin, the President of Iran, as well as leaders from Brazil and South Africa,” he said.
Meanwhile, in another development, he said J-KOM, the Information Department (JAPEN) and the National Information Dissemination Centre (NADI) would work together strategically to strengthen the delivery of government information and policies directly to grassroots communities.
He said the collaboration would create more effective and comprehensive synergies in information dissemination to ensure that every government initiative and policy is optimally understood by the people.
“We deliver information and, at the same time, we gather feedback from the grassroots. This approach ensures that the issues addressed are truly targeted, based on findings obtained directly from the grassroots,” he added. — Bernama

Title: FDS crash: Dr Ainul’s husband thanks all, calls nationwide support a ‘blessing’
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — The husband of helicopter crash victim Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin has expressed his appreciation to all those who assisted with and prayed for the smooth handling of his wife’s remains.
Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, 37, said the support from the federal, Sarawak and Kelantan governments had greatly helped facilitate arrangements concerning his late wife, including throughout his time in Sarawak.
“Fate has taken its course, but
Alhamdulillah
, everything was made easier. I received support from everyone, both friends and people who did not know me.
“For me, that was a blessing for the deceased, as she received the support and prayers of Malaysians nationwide. Thank you to everyone, including the media,” he told reporters when met at Masjid Al Karomah Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here today.
He said arrangements in Sarawak had proceeded smoothly although they took some time, with some uncertainty surrounding the information available in the initial stages.
“However, it was all right because everything was completed earlier than expected, including the identification process and DNA testing.
“I accept what has happened, but there are times when memories and thoughts of her come back to me,” he said, his voice breaking with emotion.
Dr Ainul Baraah, 33, was laid to rest at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery at 2.20pm today following funeral prayers at Masjid Al Karomah Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa.
She was among five people killed in a Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash at the Long Lellang STOLport in Baram last Tuesday. — Bernama

Title: MOH to review all FDS helicopter contracts, RM30 flight allowance after fatal Sarawak crash
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will review all contracts related to helicopter services for the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) following the crash of an FDS helicopter in Long Lellang, Baram, Sarawak, last Tuesday.
Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said the review would cover all aspects of the contracts, including matters related to FDS, in line with instructions from Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the RM30 allowance paid to FDS personnel for each flight would also be reviewed as part of the exercise.
Mahathar declined to comment on claims that the helicopter involved in the crash was old, saying the matter was under investigation by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
“As mentioned in the press conference issued by the Honourable Minister, we will review all the contracts related to it... everything will be reviewed,” he told reporters after officiating the Malaysian Trauma Conference (MTC) 2026 here today.
Five people were killed when the FDS helicopter carrying an MOH team crashed and caught fire near the end of the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram last Tuesday.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham and four MOH personnel: Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, and nurses Jessie Paya Jok and Debra Moset.
Following the crash, MOH announced that FDS operations in Sarawak would be temporarily suspended to allow a comprehensive assessment of the service's safety and operational mechanisms.
The assessment covers the FDS delivery framework, including contracts, governance, operational safety, coverage requirements and the effectiveness of the existing service model. — Bernama

Title: EC to review electoral boundaries nationwide if Parliament approves more Sabah, Sarawak seats
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — The Election Commission (EC) will conduct a review of electoral constituency boundaries, subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said it took note of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s statement on Friday on the proposed amendments to the Federal Constitution to allow for an increase in the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak.
The increase in parliamentary seats will also take into account the electoral constituencies in Peninsular Malaysia, based on the principle that the ratio of representation for Sabah and Sarawak will also be increased from the current level.
“In the context of the delineation of electoral constituencies in the three study units, the EC will conduct a review of the electoral constituency boundaries, subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution,” he said in a statement today.
He said the EC would provide further clarification once an official decision had been made and there were developments that could be announced to the public. — Bernama

Title: Police, RMAF among four agencies supporting Sarawak during Flying Doctor Service suspension
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Four enforcement agencies will assist the Ministry of Health (MOH) in carrying out mercy flights to aid people in remote areas of Sarawak who require medical assistance.
The four agencies are the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), and the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM).
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said this service would be utilised for the time being until the investigation into the incident involving the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter is concluded.
“The mobilised alternatives include securing assistance from JBPM through its Emergency Medical Air Rescue Services (EMARS).
“As I mentioned in a previous statement, we have already mobilised these measures and other alternatives,” he said when met by reporters after accompanying the remains of Dr. Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here today.
He stated that the ministry could not allow the service to remain suspended for too long, while simultaneously aiming to strengthen safety-related aspects.
“MOH is awaiting the investigation findings from the authorities before determining the next steps to enhance safety and enable the resumption of FDS operations.
“Seven MOH FDS teams provide services to approximately 14,000 to 15,000 residents in remote areas that are difficult to access via conventional routes,” he said.
On Tuesday, five individuals on board a BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace lost their lives after the aircraft crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3:40pm.
In addition to Dr. Ainul Baraah, the other fatalities were Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham (30), medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry (31), and two nurses, Jessie Paya Jok (44) and Debra Moset (40). — Bernama

Title: Anwar: 1MDB recovery about restoring trust amid RM4.2b claim against Singapore’s DBS
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Finance (MoF) has taken note of a compensation claim amounting to approximately RM4.2 billion filed by four companies against DBS Bank Ltd at the Singapore High Court.
The four companies, which are currently undergoing liquidation under court-appointed liquidators, are seeking damages related to funds allegedly misappropriated from 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and SRC International Sdn Bhd.
“The recovery efforts are not merely about reclaiming the money that was lost.
“Trust, confidence in institutions and Malaysia’s standing in the eyes of its international partners were also compromised in this dark chapter of the nation’s history,” said Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in a media statement today.
He also said that the Madani Government is committed to strengthening institutional governance and accountability to ensure that such a betrayal does not happen again.
The MoF statement also said that, according to the 1MDB Asset Recovery Task Force, the claim involves five DBS accounts opened in 2013 by the four companies.
The account-opening documents named Tan Kim Loong, also known as Eric Tan, as the sole beneficial owner of the companies and the signatory for all five accounts.
The accounts were allegedly used to channel more than US$1 billion (RM4.07 billion) in misappropriated 1MDB and SRC funds between 2013 and 2014.
“Based on the latest figures, the total amount of 1MDB obligations borne by the government stands at RM51.4 billion, comprising RM42.5 billion already paid by the government and an outstanding debt of RM8.9 billion.
“A total of RM31.3 billion has been received through asset recovery efforts, leaving the government to bear potential losses of RM20 billion as a result of the 1MDB scandal,” the MoF said.
The recovery efforts involve cooperation and legal proceedings in several countries, including the United States, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and Singapore.
Among the latest recoveries was the settlement reached by the government with JPMorganChase in August 2025, involving a RM1.4 billion contribution to the Malaysian Asset Recovery Trust Account.
Funds recovered through the account are used to repay debts and meet existing financial obligations related to 1MDB and SRC, thereby reducing the burden on public finances. — Bernama

Title: Health Minister leads funeral prayers for helicopter crash victim Dr Ainul Baraah
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad led the funeral prayers for medical officer, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here at 1.37 pm today.
The prayers were attended by over 1,000 congregants, including Ministry of Health (MOH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan State Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased’s family members and friends.
The deceased’s father, Kamarudin Salleh, 69, said he and his family had granted permission for Dr Dzulkefly to lead the funeral prayers as a mark of respect.
“I wish to express my gratitude to the Health Minister and the public—including relatives and friends—for their constant prayers and for keeping my late daughter in their thoughts,” he said.
Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah’s remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at Sultan Ismail Petra Airport, Pengkalan Chepa, at 11.21 am.
The crash on Tuesday claimed the lives of all five individuals on board the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at approximately 3.40 pm.
In addition to Dr Ainul Baraah, the other victims were Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and two nurses, Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40. — Bernama

Title: Fisherman missing after falling into sea near Pulau Batu Layang found dead
Article:
KANGAR, Sept 13 — The body of a fisherman who fell into the sea while fishing near Pulau Batu Layang, Sungai Baru here yesterday, was found about 400 metres from the island today.
The victim was identified as Khairul Amir Bahroom, 33, who was reported missing at about 3.30 am yesterday while out at sea with his elder brother.
Kuala Perlis Maritime Zone director Maritime Commander Nak Rong A/L Si Prom said the body was discovered by local fishermen and the finding was reported to the search and rescue operation team this morning.
“The operation team received information from the fishing community about the discovery of a body approximately 400 metres from Pulau Batu Layang,” he said in a statement today.
He said Bot Benteng 1207 subsequently retrieved the body and brought it to the Kuala Perlis Customs Jetty before handing it over to police for further action.
Kangar District Police Chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop confirmed that the body would be taken to the Forensic Unit of Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) for a post-mortem. — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry preparing for possible rise in public hospital patients amid soaring insurance costs
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is constantly planning and projecting healthcare service requirements to prepare for a possible increase in the number of patients at public hospitals amid rising health insurance costs.
Director-General of Health Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said such planning and projections formed part of the public healthcare sector’s day-to-day and long-term planning, including financial requirements to meet changes in demand for healthcare services.
“In the healthcare sector, particularly the public sector, we make projections as part of our day-to-day and long-term planning to anticipate what may happen and so on.
“These projections form one of the bases for planning and government financial support to ensure healthcare service needs can be met,” he told reporters after officiating the Malaysian Trauma Conference (MTC) 2026 here today.
He was responding to reports quoting KSI Strategic Institute for Asia Pacific president Tan Sri Michael Yeoh as saying that health insurance costs, which have risen by up to 20 per cent annually, were becoming increasingly worrying and required serious attention to prevent the financial burden on the public from worsening.
Dr Mahathar said the ministry was also aware of concerns over reported increases of up to 20 per cent annually in health insurance costs, which could place a greater financial burden on the public and affect demand for public healthcare services.
He said MOH and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) were working together through a joint committee to look into the issue, including the government’s Medi-Asas programme, an insurance and takaful medical protection plan designed to provide Malaysians with access to more affordable and sustainable health coverage.
“As for insurance and related matters, these fall more under the purview of other agency that regulate aspects such as premiums,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar confirms Malaysia exploring acquisition of India’s BrahMos missile system
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Malaysia is exploring the possibility of acquiring India’s BrahMos air-to-surface missile system, while emphasising that discussions are still ongoing and no final decision has been made.
In an interview with India’s
NDTV,
he said discussion on it took place during the bilateral meeting with his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, but the rightful decision maker would be Malaysia’s Air Force.
“(We) did discuss, but normally my position is always to get the departments or agencies concerned, those having the expertise in the Air Force, they should then continue.
“They have had initial discussions and I told Prime Minister Modi that I am very supportive of that because this relationship is build on trust and we want to cement it in all fields,” he said.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, acknowledged India’s defence capabilities.
The BrahMos is a long-range, ramjet-powered supersonic cruise missile that can be launched from submarines, ships, fighter aircraft or transporter erector launcher.
It is a joint venture between India’s Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Russian Federation’s NPO Mashinostroyeniya, who together formed BrahMos Aerospace. — Bernama

Title: Construction of Cameron Highlands bypass yet to begin, suspension calls premature, says Works Ministry
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Works (KKR) has taken note of media reports and concerns raised regarding flash floods and landslides in Cameron Highlands, including calls for the temporary suspension of the Cameron Highlands Bypass Project.
In a statement today, the Public Works Department (JKR) explained that the project involves the construction of the Tanah Rata Bypass, the upgrading of Federal Road FT59 from Tanah Rata to Kea Farm, and the upgrading of Federal Road FT434 (Jalan Griddle).
“At present, the project remains in the design and assessment study stage. To date, no physical construction work related to the project has been carried out on-site, with the exception of routine maintenance on existing roads.
“Therefore, any claims linking the flash flood incident to the project's physical construction activities are inaccurate,” the statement read.
According to the Public Works Department (JKR), preliminary checks revealed that the flooding reported yesterday in the Taman MARDI and Padang Awam areas of Tanah Rata, Cameron Highlands, occurred on secondary roads; these locations are not part of the main road alignment involved in the project.
However, a small-scale landslide did occur on Jalan Tengkolok, an area falling under the scope of the project contractor's routine maintenance duties.
“Debris clearing operations were carried out immediately and have been completed to ensure the safety and smooth flow of traffic for road users,” the statement added.
The Ministry of Works (KKR) takes all concerns regarding slope safety, geological conditions, drainage systems, and disaster risks seriously.
The project's implementation is subject to all assessments, approvals, and technical conditions stipulated by relevant authorities, including the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), Social Impact Assessment (SIA), geotechnical requirements, and local authority approvals.
The statement noted that physical construction work would only commence once all relevant approvals and conditions have been met. — Bernama

Title: Teen among 146 detained in road bully operation at Bukit Raja toll plaza
Article:
KLANG, Sept 13 — A 16-year-old teenager was among 146 individuals detained for checks during an operation targeting road bullies at the Bukit Raja Toll Plaza on the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) here early today.
Sinar Harian
reported that the integrated operation involving the Selangor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT), Road Transport Department (JPJ) and National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) also resulted in 50 motorcycles being seized for various offences.
In a statement, Selangor police said 146 individuals aged between 16 and 25, as well as 141 motorcycles, were inspected during the operation.
“Selangor police issued 92 summonses, while the Bukit Aman JSPT issued 24 summonses for various traffic offences,” the statement said.
A total of 50 motorcycles were also seized for further action.
Meanwhile, AADK conducted 22 random urine screening tests involving 17 men and five women.
“The screening found that no individuals were arrested for testing positive for drugs,” the statement said.

Title: Motorcyclist dies after trying to avoid pedestrian in Hulu Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — A 60-year-old motorcyclist died after he reportedly tried to avoid a pedestrian crossing the road before falling and being run over by a lorry in Hulu Selangor yesterday.
Sinar Harian reported that the incident occurred at about 7pm along Jalan Batang Kali-Ulu Yam, citing Hulu Selangor district police chief Supt M Manimaran.
Manimaran said preliminary investigations found that the victim was believed to have been overtaking a lorry from the right when a pedestrian was crossing the road.
“The motorcyclist is believed to have tried to avoid the pedestrian before losing control and falling from his motorcycle,” he said in a statement today.
The victim was then run over by the lorry, which was driven by a 45-year-old man travelling to Penang to deliver goods.
Manimaran said the victim was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer.
Police received information about the fatal accident at about 7.30pm through the Traffic Complaints Counter.
He said further investigations were underway to determine the exact cause of the accident.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Manimaran also urged anyone with information on the incident to contact traffic investigation officer Insp Khairul Salleh Abd Rahman at 03-6064 1222 or any nearby police station to assist investigations.

Title: Health Ministry seeks to close trauma care gaps between peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to develop a more integrated national trauma network to ensure patients receive the right care, at the right place and at the right time, regardless of where they are in Malaysia.
Director-General of Health Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said the initiative was important to ensure a more interconnected trauma care system while narrowing access gaps between urban and rural areas, as well as Sabah and Sarawak.
He said the trauma chain of survival must be strengthened comprehensively, from bystander response and first aid at the scene to pre-hospital emergency medical services and transportation, resuscitation at the Emergency Department, definitive trauma care and rehabilitation.
“The chain is only as strong as its weakest link. We need seamless coordination across all these stages, with the right skills, adequate resources and the right system working together as one continuum of care,” he said when launching the Malaysian Trauma Conference (MTC) 2026 here today.
He said access to quality trauma care should not depend on a patient’s location, as every Malaysian deserved timely and appropriate trauma care.
Meanwhile, he said up to 30 per cent of trauma deaths were considered preventable based on the first National Trauma Registry report published in 2008.
Dr Mahathar, who was among the report’s co-authors, said the situation highlighted the need for a comprehensive transformation of the country’s trauma care system, stressing that “in trauma, every second, every minute counts”.
He said trauma remained a major public health challenge, particularly among the younger and working-age population, with transport-related injuries continuing to be a major contributor to preventable deaths.
He added that trauma care was also becoming increasingly complex as Malaysia moved towards an ageing population, with more patients presenting with multiple non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular disease.
“These NCDs significantly influence how patients respond to trauma, how quickly they deteriorate and how they recover. Therefore, we can no longer look at trauma care in isolation,” he said.
Dr Mahathar said the National Trauma Transformation Conference Roadshow (NTTR) 2025-2026, involving six locations across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, was implemented to address these challenges systematically by aligning local clinical practices with global benchmarks, sharing best practices and promoting continuous quality improvement.
He stressed that MOH’s challenge now was not merely to produce policies and guidelines, but to translate them into effective and actionable implementation plans.
“Our challenge is not about producing policies and guidelines. Our challenge is translating policies and guidelines into actionable implementation plans. In trauma management, this is not an option,” he said.
He said strengthening trauma care also required a whole-of-society approach involving government agencies, the private sector, NGOs, academia and local communities, with the focus extending beyond treatment to injury prevention.
“This includes strengthening injury prevention, safety advocacy, public education and targeted interventions, particularly for road traffic and occupational injuries. Prevention must be an integral part of our national trauma strategy,” he said.
He added that the ultimate goal was to ensure that when a serious injury occurred, the system was ready, healthcare personnel were prepared, services were connected and patients received the care they needed without delay. — Bernama

Title: Police investigate death of 15-year-old girl after fall from Putrajaya apartment
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — Police are investigating the death of a 15-year-old girl who was found on the ground of an apartment in Precinct 5 here after she was believed to have fallen from a high floor of the building, Putrajaya District Police Chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said today.
He said police received a call about the incident at 10.33pm yesterday and the girl was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer from Putrajaya Hospital.
“Preliminary investigations found that the 15-year-old girl was found lying down, believed to have fallen from a high place. The victim lived with her family on the ninth floor of the apartment,” he said when contacted by Bernama.
An autopsy will be conducted today, while the case has been classified as sudden death pending further investigation.
“The cause of the incident is still under investigation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Health Minister: FDS crash victims’ remains handed over to families after DNA identification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The remains of the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, Sarawak, were handed over to their respective families this morning at the Forensic Department of Miri Hospital after their identities were confirmed through DNA analysis.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the Ministry of Health (MOH) coordinated the transportation of the remains to their respective final resting places following official confirmation of their identities by the police and the Department of Chemistry.
He said the remains of medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin will be flown from Miri to Kota Bharu, Kelantan on a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft before being buried at Seri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery, Kampung Baung, Pengkalan Chepa.
“The remains of nurse Debra Moset will be laid to rest at Kampung Semadang, Padawan tomorrow, while nurse Jessie Paya Jok’s remains will be taken to her home today, with her funeral to be held at BEM Cemetery Lambir, Miri tomorrow.
“The remains of assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry would be taken to his family home today, with the funeral scheduled for Tuesday (Sept 15) at Anglican Cemetery Lambir, Miri,” he said in a statement.
He said the remains of pilot Capt Zainol Afiq Bee Sham will be flown from Miri to Kuala Lumpur International Airport on a Malaysia Airlines flight before being buried at Forest Heights Muslim Cemetery, Senawang, Negeri Sembilan.
Dzulkefly expressed his appreciation to the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) for providing logistical support through the RMAF to facilitate the repatriation of the remains to Peninsular Malaysia.
He also thanked the police, Department of Chemistry, Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Sarawak Islamic Religious Department (JAIS), Miri Hospital management and all agencies involved, from the search and rescue (SAR) operation through to the handling of the remains.
Meanwhile, he said the ministry would continue to strengthen its strategic cooperation with JBPM to support the smooth implementation of medical evacuation (MEDEVAC) operations following the temporary suspension of FDS services to facilitate investigations, review and a comprehensive assessment.
He also expressed his appreciation to Malaysians for their concern, prayers and support for healthcare personnel and the victims’ families. — Bernama

Title: Police shoot at car after couple allegedly try to ram traffic officers, detained within 24 hours
Article:
KULAI, Sept — Police fired one shot at the tyre of a car after a 23-year-old couple allegedly rammed a police motorcycle and tried to hit officers during an incident in Jalan Kenari, Bandar Putra, Kulai, early yesterday.
Kulai District Police Chief ACP Tan Seng Lee said the incident occurred at about 1.20 am when members of the district police headquarters’ Motorcycle Patrol Unit (URB) stopped a black Perodua Myvi in the area after finding it suspicious, with a local man and woman inside the vehicle.
“During the inspection, the suspects became aggressive and tried to flee by ramming the URB motorcycle and a public vehicle, a Mazda CX-5, besides attempting to hit the police officers.
“Following this, the URB personnel fired one shot at the tyre of the suspects’ vehicle to defend themselves and stop the vehicle. However, the suspects managed to escape,” he said in a statement today.
He said a URB officer suffered minor injuries to his leg after becoming trapped when the police motorcycle was struck by the suspects’ vehicle.
Tan said within 24 hours of the incident, Kulai police arrested the male and female suspects separately in Bandar Putra, Kulai and Kluang between 11.30 am and 8.30 pm yesterday.
Police also seized the black Perodua Myvi believed to have been used in the incident, along with a remote control.
Tan said preliminary urine screening tests on both suspects were negative, while checks found that neither had a previous criminal record.
“The motive for the incident is still under investigation. The case is being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder, Section 332 for voluntarily causing hurt to a public servant and Section 186 for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties,” he said.
Both suspects will be brought before the Johor Bahru Magistrates’ Court today for a remand application. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Egypt’s El-Sisi to make official visit to Malaysia next month
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi is scheduled to make an official visit to Malaysia next month.
“Insya-Allah, several matters concerning Malaysia-Egypt relations will be discussed in greater depth during President El-Sisi’s official visit to Malaysia next month,” he said in a post on his social media today.
No further details on the visit were provided in the post.
El-Sisi was among the leaders Anwar met on the sidelines of a gala dinner held in conjunction with the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here yesterday.
In 2024, Malaysia and Egypt agreed to work towards elevating bilateral relations to a strategic partnership.
Anwar arrived here yesterday to attend the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit, which concludes today.
The Prime Minister will continue his working visit to Keralam (officially renamed from Kerala), a state on the Malabar Coast of southern India.
This is Anwar’s second official visit to India, following his inaugural trip as Prime Minister in August 2024.
The Prime Minister will then depart for the Maldives tomorrow (Sept 14). — AFP
